Le parc est presque entièrement situé au: The park lies almost entirely in Nord-Kivu, but its northernmost part belongs to Irumu territory, now in Ituri, and Tshegera Island belongs to Kalehe territory in Sud-Kivu. The 2018 UNESCO/IUCN report, p. 8, gives 98.83% in Nord-Kivu, 1.13% in Irumu (still called Province Orientale) and 48 ha on Tshegera. These small portions are part of the park; its provincial classification should not be limited to access from Goma.
Le siège et la zone touristique se trouv: The headquarters and tourist area are near Bukavu in Sud-Kivu; the full park also extends into Nord-Kivu and Maniema according to its official manager, ICCN/WCS.
Le parc s’étend sur quatre provinces act: The park extends across four current provinces. Tshuapa belonged to the former province of Équateur; Équateur should not be used to refer to this part of the park today.
Maniema et Tshopo désignent ici le parc: Maniema and Tshopo refer here to the national park itself, following the brochure from its founding TL2 project and an ICCN call issued in 2024. Sources differ: the 2026 ANAPI booklet (p. 24) adds Lomami province and gives an outdated area; the tentative-list entry submitted by the DRC to UNESCO in 2024 adds Sankuru. These additions have not been retained because their inclusion within the park boundary is unconfirmed; the Tshuapa and Lualaba river basins and the buffer zone are not synonymous with the provinces crossed by the park.
Le parc entier s’étend sur trois provinc: According to its manager, the full park extends across three provinces: Haut-Katanga, Haut-Lomami and Lualaba. Lualaba alone, mentioned in the ANAPI booklet, does not represent its full extent.
Le gestionnaire situe le domaine dans la: The manager places the estate in the commune of Maluku, within the city-province of Kinshasa.
Rattachement au Kongo Central du site de: The Inkisi falls site belongs to Kongo Central; it should be distinguished from the city of Zongo in Sud-Ubangi.
